title: Cultured & Low-Alcohol Ferments (SCOBY & Grain Cultures)
attribution: The symbiotic-culture ferments — kombucha, water and milk kefir, jun — sit at the boundary of alcoholic and soft drink: most finish under 1% ABV, but sealed or extended ferments cross into it, which is why several jurisdictions regulate high-ABV kombucha as an alcoholic beverage. Documented from producer and food-science sources; values are typical.

styles.name: Kombucha
styles.impression: Fermented sweet tea — tart, vinegary, effervescent and faintly fruity, soured by a floating cellulose mat of bacteria and yeast.
styles.comments: Commercial kombucha is kept under 0.5% ABV to stay a soft drink; a sealed second fermentation ('hard kombucha') is deliberately pushed to 3–8% and regulated as alcohol. The SCOBY is the visible 'mother'.
styles.ingredients: Sweetened tea (Camellia sinensis) fermented by a SCOBY (symbiotic culture of Acetobacter and yeast). Yeast makes alcohol; bacteria convert most of it to acetic acid.

styles.name: Jun
styles.impression: A green-tea-and-honey cousin of kombucha — lighter, more delicate and wine-like, fermented by its own honey-adapted culture.
styles.comments: Often marketed with a Himalayan origin myth; more likely a modern honey-adapted kombucha. Ferments cooler and faster than kombucha.
styles.ingredients: Green tea sweetened with honey (not sugar), fermented by a jun SCOBY.

styles.name: Water Kefir / Tibicos
styles.impression: A dairy-free fizzy ferment — light, lemonade-like and mildly tart — bubbled up by translucent 'grains' in sugar water.
styles.comments: Tibicos, water-kefir grains, California bees, ginger-beer plant — related SCOBY-like cultures. Finishes low in alcohol; sealed bottles build both fizz and a little more.
styles.ingredients: Sugar water (often with dried fruit and lemon) fermented by tibicos grains, a symbiotic community of lactic bacteria and yeast in a polysaccharide matrix.

styles.name: Milk Kefir
styles.impression: Cultured milk — tart, creamy, faintly yeasty and lightly effervescent, the Caucasus's contribution to the world's ferment shelf.
styles.comments: Originates in the North Caucasus. Usually treated as a food; extended or warm ferments raise the alcohol and carbonation noticeably.
styles.ingredients: Milk fermented by kefir grains, a symbiotic matrix of lactic bacteria and yeast. The yeast fraction makes it lightly alcoholic and fizzy, unlike yoghurt.
